hook: The lights go out. The U P S takes over. And the clock starts ticking.
stat1: Power is still the leading cause of outages that hurt the business.
intro: Here is how Mova iO keeps a site running through a power cut.
s1: Nine forty-one. In Ops Ramp, the Vadodara office loses utility power. The U P S goes on battery, and the generator switch reports that it hasn't transferred. Mova iO groups it all into one inference.
s2: On the U P S management card, the battery is at ninety-two percent, carrying sixty-one percent load. That leaves thirty-eight minutes.
s3: The agent checks the utility's outage page. It's a cable fault, with power expected back in about two hours. So the battery will not last, and the generator has to run.
s4: A priority one incident opens in ServiceNow with the plan already in it: shed non-critical load to buy time, get the generator started by hand, and send an engineer to fix the switch.
s5: Facilities has already been called. Site I T approves the load shedding in Teams, keeping the domain controller, the file server and C C T V running.
s6: In v Center, five non-critical machines shut down cleanly: print, test, two V D I hosts, and the update server.
s7: The load drops to thirty-four percent, and the runtime nearly doubles, to seventy-one minutes. At ten oh two, Facilities starts the generator, and the U P S goes back on line.
s8: In Field Service, the nearest engineer with the right skills and parts is already on the way. And the site updates channel gets a plain-language status, with what's off and when power should be back.
close: Battery stretched from thirty-eight to seventy-one minutes. Generator running twenty-one minutes after the cut. No servers dropped, and the engineer already on the way.
tag: Power cuts, handled by Mova iO agents. With people in control.
end: Movate. Your applied A I partner.
